subject: Follow-up: Hosting route & evidence needed for HIPAA workflows
messages:
From: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.ai>
To: Emma Thompson <emma.thompson@pulsewell.health>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-08-22T15:05:00-07:00
Subject: Follow-up: Hosting route & evidence needed for HIPAA workflows

Hi Emma — thanks again for the call earlier today. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have alignment on the hosting path that meets PulseWell's compliance bar.

Summary of requirements you shared:
- PHI workload handling under HIPAA; need a signed BAA before production traffic.
- Evidence of SOC 2 Type II controls (attestation/report) — security and availability focus.
- Customer-managed keys required for encryption at-rest (KMS/HSM integration).
- Data residency: US-only processing and logs retention for 7+ years for auditability.
- Audit support: ability to surface logs and provide evidence for encryption, access controls, and change management.

Hosting options we discussed (high-level tradeoffs):
1) Hosted API (Redwood hosted) + BAA: fastest time-to-value. We can sign a BAA and provide SOC 2 report copies; however, KMS integration is limited to bring-your-own-key (BYOK) via specific cloud partners and may require Dedicated tenancy for full separation.
2) Dedicated capacity (reserved GPU pools) in our Dedicated offering: predictable throughput and stronger isolation; supports BYOK and extended logging; recommended if you want near-hosted speed with improved control.
3) Private VPC / on-prem package: highest control and auditability (customer network, KMS/HSM inside your environment). Longer lead time and requires ops coordination.

Requested action items / questions for PulseWell:
- Which hosting route do you prefer to evaluate first? (Hosted + BAA / Dedicated / Private VPC)
- Can you confirm the internal security contact who will own the questionnaire and the target date for the audit window?
- Do you have a copy of your standard vendor security questionnaire (or a pointer to your InfoSec portal)? I attached a short evidence checklist (redwood-hipaa-evidence-checklist.pdf) and a mutual-action-plan template to the email.

Proposed Redwood owners for next steps:
- Olga Petrov (me) — technical and compliance coordination, evidence mapping.
- Marissa Cole — commercial and contracting.
- Ben Carter — infra architecture / Dedicated onboarding details.

Suggested timeline (ballpark):
- 1 week: confirm route and hand off questionnaire.
- 2–4 weeks: assemble SOC2/BAA evidence and run a tech deep-dive (if Dedicated or Private).
- 4–8 weeks: Dedicated onboarding; Private VPC/on-prem longer depending on customer infra readiness.

If you prefer, we can run a short technical deep dive with Ben next week to walk through KMS options and logging exports.

Thanks — looking forward to next steps.

Best,
Olga Petrov
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
olga.petrov@redwood.ai
+1 (415) 555-0138

Thanks Olga — this is exactly the kind of recap we need. A few clarifications from our side: 

- PulseWell MUST have a signed BAA prior to any PHI processing.
- SOC 2 Type II report: we need the latest 12-month attestation (security + availability).
- Preferred deployment: our InfoSec team prefers Private VPC or on-prem, but we are open to Dedicated if BYOK and full audit logging are available. Hosted (multi-tenant) is acceptable only if we can get strong contractual controls + BYOK and logs kept in a customer-specific bucket.
- KMS requirement: keys must be under our control; integrations with AWS KMS or Azure Key Vault are preferred. HSM certifications are a plus.
- Audit timing: we anticipate a vendor audit window in Q1 2027 and need evidence delivered by end of Dec 2026 to plan.
- I'll share our vendor security questionnaire (attached: pulsewell-security-q-ref.docx) — please map the sections to Redwood evidence points.

Also — can you provide a ballpark for Dedicated onboarding (cost and time) vs Private VPC (lift & shift effort)? That will help our procurement team.

Appreciate the quick turn on the MAP and the checklist.

—Emma

Emma — thanks for the clarifications. Below is an action plan and immediate deliverables from Redwood.

Action plan (next 30 days):
1) Evidence mapping (Olga) — we'll map your questionnaire to specific Redwood artifacts: SOC 2 report, controls matrix, encryption architecture, logging exports, and BAA clauses. Deliverable: mapped spreadsheet + links to reports by 2026-09-03.
2) BAA draft (Marissa) — BAA draft to be shared within 5 business days after you confirm hosting preference.
3) Technical deep dive (Ben + Olga) — schedule a 60-min session to review BYOK options, KMS integrations, and logging exports. Proposed slots: Wed 2026-09-01 09:00–11:00 PT or Thu 2026-09-02 13:00–15:00 PT. Please confirm preferred time.
4) High-level cost/time estimates (Ben) — Ben will provide a short table comparing Dedicated vs Private VPC (cost bands + estimated onboarding time) by 2026-08-27.

Notes on tradeoffs (short):
- Hosted + BAA: quickest; limited BYOK flexibility unless combined with Dedicated tenancy. Good if you prioritize time-to-market.
- Dedicated: strong isolation, supports BYOK and extended logging; typical onboarding 2–6 weeks depending on GPU pool sizing and security ops coordination.
- Private VPC/on-prem: most control; longer lead time (4–12+ weeks) and requires networking/KMS coordination on your side.

Attachments included: redwood-hipaa-evidence-checklist.pdf (evidence mapping template), mutual-action-plan.xlsx (MAP), and the PulseWell questionnaire you shared (pulsewell-security-q-ref.docx) — we'll start mapping today.

If we get confirmation today on preferred route, Marissa will kick off the BAA draft and Ben will send the Dedicated vs Private VPC summary.

Best regards,
